newsitem.title: GREECE: Commercial sells stake in Bank of Attica.
newsitem.headline: Commercial sells stake in Bank of Attica.

text.p: Commercial Bank, Greece's second largest state bank, sold a 49.5 percent stake in its subsidiary Bank of Attica to the pension fund of Greece's civil engineers (TSMEDE) and the state escrow fund (TPD).

"The expansion of the Bank of Attica's shareholder base with two new strategic investors who are willing and capable of expanding the bank's operations into new fields is a particularly positive development," Commercial Bank said in a statement.
According to the deal, Commercial will retain a stake of around 20 percent in Bank of Attica. It placed 34 percent with TSMEDE and 15.5 percent with TPD.

According to information disclosed in December 1996 by National Economy Minister Yiannos Papandoniou and verified by Reuters with Commercial Bank sources, Commercial will pocket a total of 6.46 billion drachmas from the sale.
This price tag translates into a per share price of 937 drachmas for Bank of Attica stock.
No further details were disclosed regarding the timing of the transfer of the shares on the Athens bourse.
Commercial said it would continue to support the Bank of Attica, assuming management for a five-year period.
A share capital increase for the Bank of Attica is also in the cards, Commercial said.
Bank of Attica shares closed down 70 drachmas at 1,385 on Friday, on volume of 41,150 shares. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
